_comment: KESTREL-2 master design parameters. The simulator (sim/), Blender CAD generator (cad/) and firmware tools all read this file. Lengths in mm, masses in g. Component z is measured from the nose tip, positive towards the tail.
name: KESTREL-2

airframe.tube: Estes BT-70 (56.3 mm OD), two 19.5 in (495 mm) tubes cut to 340 mm and 380 mm

part_names.lower: bottom part: TVC, fins, flight computer, battery, camera
part_names.upper: middle part: payload bay (door) / wall / parachute section with top release latch

airframe.finish_note: printed parts sanded 240->400 grit, filler primer, spray paint ('regular paint' ~30 um, OpenRocket default)

nose.note: printed; its base sleeve (body OD) slides over the latch insert at the top of the middle tube and pops off at apogee

leg.note: fin tips extend 30 mm below the tail so the rocket stands on its four fins; each leg tapers from 15 mm to an 11 x 7.5 mm foot

tab.note: trailing-edge tab on every fin, turned directly by the MG90S inside the fin (its shaft is the hinge line); stock horn glued into the tab
tab.linkage_note: direct drive: servo angle = tab angle (horn_mm = servo_arm_mm); linkage_cda covers the hinge gaps only

fins.thickness_note: only the bottom band (tab hinge, tab servo, lead channel; 45 mm up from the tail) is 15 mm thick; the rest of each fin is a normal 4 mm fin with a half-round leading edge, joined to the band by a 20 mm wedge (15 deg). The tab and the band end in 1.5 mm trailing edges 12 mm below the tail

tvc.motor_diameter_note: 29 mm mount for the TSP F35; 24 mm motors (D20, E20) fit with the printed adapter sleeve and their own retainer
tvc.linkage_note: gimbal deg per servo deg = horn hole radius 9 mm / gimbal arm 22 mm (CAD-checked; 18 mm on the 24 mm mount)

recovery.deploy: nose cone pushed off by a compression spring when the single snap-in latch bolt is pulled by a servo at the top
recovery.note: 36 in Estes rip-stop (302249). A 30 in gave 5.8 m/s mean and up to 7.1 m/s landings at the thick-fin mass (24 in gave 6.7 m/s at the old mass). Packs to ~44 x 90 mm (1.44 x the 30 in pack by canopy area)

launch.target_note: asked for 200 m; agreed: the F35 with the airframe as it is (about 190 m). 123 m was the original E20 estimate

components.name: printed_parts
components.note: masses/positions from cad/mass_properties.json (generated from the Blender CAD)

components.name: servo_MG90S_with_horn
components.note: MG90S 13.4 g incl. 25 cm lead + horn and screws; one entry per servo, position from the CAD

components.name: pushrods_1.2mm
components.note: TVC pushrods only (the fin tabs are driven directly)

components.name: servo_extension_tab
components.note: 15 cm servo extension each (the lead runs through the fin channel, then up the TVC frame)

components.name: servo_extension_release
components.note: 30 cm extension + routing clips; plug sits at the middle/bottom joint

components.name: parachute_36in_nylon
components.note: Estes 302249; 24 g (30 in) x canopy-area ratio 1.44

components.name: nose_ballast_M3_nuts_epoxy
components.note: about 90 M3 nuts (0.33 g each) + 3 g epoxy in the nose tip; with the 36 in chute it gives +0.83..+0.96 cal (the 15 mm fins alone had left +0.39). The balance test (BUILD_GUIDE) sets the real amount

_cad_notes: Blender Z = distance above the aft end of the lower body tube (mm). Avionics band (4 mm) sits between lower and upper tubes.

camera_pod.note: external pod, lens axis 1.5 mm outside the tube; frontal area = width x protrusion (drag model)

payload.note: payload bay = lower section of the middle part, under the wall; side door with a hinge + quarter-turn latch. The simulator adds the payload at the bay floor (nominal 25 g, max 50 g)

battery.note: JST-PH balance lead -> Overlander JST-PH to JST-XH adapter lead into the board
